Architecture: Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder with autoregressive Transformer decoder.
Datasets:
SRORIE Dataset , IAM Handwriting dataset

text recognition benchmarks
Performance:
TrOCR achieved significantly higher scores than traditional and modular models.

Achieved a Character Error Rate (CER) of 3.42 while the LARGE version had a 
CER score of 2.89 which was lowest till then. TrOCR established five new state-of-the-art results out of the eight experiments when fine-tuned with synthetic and benchmark data
Strengths:
Ease of Implementation and Maintenance:
Its streamlined design avoids complex, multi-stage pre-processing or post-processing steps. It can also be easily 
extended for multilingual recognition by swapping in a multilingual pre-trained decoder and expanding the dictionary
Industrial Efficiency: The model family includes a SMALL variant (62M parameters) that provides comparable accuracy to larger versions while being twice as fast, making it ideal for industrial deployment where compute resources are limited
Weaknesses:
Sensitivity to Symbol Consistency: The model can underperform on datasets where the visual symbols present in an image are omitted from the ground truth (e.g., the IIIT5K dataset)
Because it is pre-trained to recognize symbols, it may truncate the output 
or substitute symbols for similar characters when trying to match the 
length expectations of certain benchmarks
Performance vs. Ground Truth Conflicts: If a document contains characters (like punctuation or symbols) that the ground truth doesn't expect, the model's tendency to process every visual signal can lead to character-level errors
Language:
It can also be easily extended for multilingual 
by swapping in a multilingual pre-trained decoder

DotsOCR currently has several compatibility issues that make 
it difficult to run outside the authors' intended environment. 
The repository assumes the presence of FlashAttention and imports it unconditionally, preventing execution on systems where it is unavailable or unsupported (e.g., NVIDIA T4 GPUs). The vision encoder also contains a hardcoded bfloat16 conversion,
